conviction_note: Nothing found that the market cannot already see: the quarter's big lines (IB and markets up mid-to-high teens) were guided on 2026-09-15 and are in consensus. The independent series I could reach (LSEG fee league tables, the Chase card trust, H.8, the Fed's September hike) mostly corroborate the guide or offset each other. The one lean is a sector de-rating driven by fund rotation into a fundamentally intact print, against a stock that sold its beats on 3 of the last 4 prints. So p_up is 54 and the move is the option-implied 3.05% nudged up to 3.2, giving +0.26. The findings sum to +0.55; the two measurements agree in sign and are both small.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $5.86-5.94 and revenue $50.8-52.2bn, from two agreeing sources: Hudson Labs, 2026-09-28, EPS $5.86 / rev $50,847M (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/jpmorgan-q3-2026-earnings-preview-revenue-guidance-outlook), and MarketPulse/Google Finance, 2026-10-07, EPS $5.91 / rev $51.15bn (https://www.marketpulse.com/markets/jpmorgan-q3-earnings-preview-can-strong-banking-momentum-continue/). Zacks reportedly has EPS $5.94 / rev $52.21bn. Company guide, from the Q2 call on 2026-07-14: FY26 NII ex-Markets ~$96.5bn, total NII ~$105.5bn, adjusted expense ~$107.5bn, card NCO ~3.2%. Q3 guide from 2026-09-15: IB fees and markets revenue up mid-to-high teens YoY on Q3'25 bases of $2.63bn and $8.9bn, which implies IB ~$3.0-3.1bn and markets ~$10.2-10.5bn. No sourced Q3 NII consensus was found; H2 run-rate arithmetic on the guide implies ~$24.7bn/quarter NII ex-Markets.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 1.06% of float with 3.4 days to cover per equibles (undated, https://equibles.com/stocks/JPM). The 2026-07-15 settlement had 29.5M shares short and 2.63 days to cover (curvedtrading, via the sweep row). Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism. Skew_25d is +1.96 vol points: mild put bid, and the baseline reads the lean as 'balanced'. Put/call OI is 0.55. Event-implied move is 3.05% (straddle 3.36%, front expiry 2026-10-16). Run-up is -4.52% over 20 days, and the stock is -8.45% from its 52-week high. MarketPulse puts the ATH at 366.50 on 2026-08-13 and a low of 325.87 on 2026-10-01, with RSI 31.6 on 09-30. Truist (via 24/7 Wall St, 2026-10-02) says financials had their worst month against the S&P since 1990, and calls it fund-flow rotation rather than results.

findings.finding: At Barclays on 2026-09-15, co-president Doug Petno guided Q3 IB fees and markets revenue up 'mid-to-high teens' YoY. On Q3'25 bases of $2.63bn IB and $8.9bn markets, that is about $3.0-3.1bn and $10.2-10.5bn. JPM has a record of printing above its September conference guide: in Q3'25 it guided IB up low double digits and printed +16%, with markets +25%. The guide is public and consensus moved up after it (Zacks EPS revised to $5.94), so this is a reported-quarter item inside the guide; only an above-guide print would be new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3'25 beat its own IB/markets guide (IB +16% vs low-double-digit guide, markets +25%) and EPS beat ($5.07 vs $4.83), yet the stock fell 1.91% on the print (baseline 2025-10-14). Q2'26: IB +30%, markets +35%, plus a raised NII guide, and the stock gained 2.5%. Beats on this line have been sold unless the guide moved.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the guide is four weeks old, the stock rose 0.7% on it, and consensus EPS ticked up. If the market expected a big upside surprise here, the 25d skew would lean to calls rather than +1.96 put-over-call, and the stock would not be 8% off its high. What remains unpriced is only JPM's habit of beating its own conference guide.
findings.independence: Q3'25 base and the prior guide-vs-print pattern: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2768224/jpm%27s-q3-earnings-beat-as-ib-%26-trading-businesses-shine-nii-view. Jefferies' Jun-Aug quarter (IB +17%, equities +29%) is a separate counterparty read, filed below.

findings.finding: LSEG fee league tables imply JPM Q3 2026 IB fees of about $3.3bn (LSEG-estimated). JPM was at $10.1bn for 9M 2026 (published 2026-10-05) against $6.8bn for H1 2026 (2026-07-06). That is an implied Q3 share of ~8.9% against 8.5% in H1, while industry fees fell sequentially in Q3. This corroborates the mid-to-high-teens guide, possibly toward its upper end. LSEG's estimates are not JPM's reported numbers, and H1 is usually revised up in later releases, which would understate the implied Q3 figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as the guide finding above; IB-fee beats on their own have not lifted the stock (Q3'25 -1.91%).
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 figure for JPM has to be derived by subtracting two LSEG releases three months apart, and nothing aggregates that number. If the share gain were priced, previews would quote a Q3 IB number above the guide; they quote only the guide.
findings.independence: The H1 base comes from a separate release of the same vendor: https://www.investmentexecutive.com/news/research-and-markets/first-half-delivers-fee-feast-for-investment-banks/ (2026-07-06). It supports the same direction as the company guide in the finding above but is a different source.

findings.finding: Chase Issuance Trust card credit was benign into Q3. Monthly net credit losses were 1.58% in July and 1.66% in August 2026, against 1.68/1.73/1.62% for April-June (Q2 card NCO rate 3.34%). Total delinquency was 0.80% in August, against 0.85% in September 2025 and 0.92% in February 2026. This is consistent with Q3 card NCOs at or below the ~3.2% FY guide, and with no reserve build driven by card credit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The card NCO guide was cut from 3.4% to 3.2% at Q2 and the stock gained 2.5% (with the NII raise). No print in the baseline window turned on card credit alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Trust data is public but rarely quoted in previews, which talk about consumer 'fragility' and macro rather than these numbers. The trust is a seasoned, prime-weighted subset that runs well below the bank-wide card NCO rate, so it confirms direction but not level. A priced read would show up as previews flagging card NCOs below guide; none do.
findings.independence: H.8 shows card/revolving balance growth slowing to +0.4% annualized in August (https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h8/20261002/), which points to low balance-driven loss growth but also slower card NII. 24/7 Wall St (2026-10-02) notes Citi's card delinquencies fell.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 by a 12-0 vote, its first hike since 2023. JPM's July NII guide (~$105.5bn total, ~$96.5bn ex-Markets) assumed the forward curve; going into the meeting a hike was priced at only ~36-52%. For an asset-sensitive balance sheet that supports holding or nudging up the FY NII guide and a higher Q4 exit rate. That would be a guidance item, but small: only part of a hike was unpriced, over 3.5 months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII guide is the line this stock trades on: July's NII raise brought +2.5%, April's guide trim -0.82% (baseline and sweep row). January 2026 -4.19% came with 2026 expense guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: Bank stocks FELL after the hike (S&P Global: bank index -6.9% from 09-16 to month-end against S&P 500 +0.9%), so the market treated the hike as a valuation and credit negative, not an NII positive. If the NII benefit were priced, JPM would not have de-rated through the hike. This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed.
findings.independence: S&P Global on banks after the hike: https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/articles/2026/10/most-us-bank-stocks-trade-lower-in-september-106462675. Pre-meeting hike odds: https://cryptobriefing.com/fomc-meeting-expected-to-result-in-first-rate-hike-since-2023-bloomberg/. Proxy, not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: Industry balance growth slowed sharply in Q3, per Fed H.8 (2026-10-02 release). Large domestic bank deposits went from $12,204bn (June) to $12,288bn (August), with September weekly values of $12,298-12,384bn: about 4% annualized, against 8.1% in Q2. Large-bank loans grew about 1% annualized June to August against 7.5% in Q2. All-bank card balances grew +0.4% annualized in August. The July NII raise rested mainly on deposit balances, so slower deposit and loan growth caps upside to NII ex-Markets, partly offsetting the rate benefit in the finding above.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII guide line: +2.5% on the July deposit-driven raise, -0.82% on the April trim.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote Q2's +7% YoY deposit growth and the raised guide, not the Q3 industry deceleration. If priced, previews would flag NII ex-Markets risk; they do not. It is an industry proxy: JPM gained wholesale deposit share in H1 and may diverge.
findings.independence: Barnum on the Q2 call called yield-seeking deposit flows 'probably a little bit of a risk' and expected consumer deposits to grow only low single digits (https://www.webull.com/news/15271033854174208). Proxy; the Fed-hike finding above pushes NII the other way through rates, not balances.

findings.finding: The sector de-rating into the print looks flow-driven, not results-driven. Financials had their worst month against the S&P since 1990 (Truist). The KBW bank index is ~13-14% off its August record, and the S&P bank index fell 6.8% in September. JPM fell ~11% from its 2026-08-13 ATH (366.50) to 325.87 on 10-01 and sits at 334.32, 8.45% off its high with a -4.52% 20-day run-up. Meanwhile the company guided Q3 capital-markets revenue up. With low short interest, the setup is light positioning into an intact print, unlike the last two prints, when the stock went in near highs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of the last four prints, the one up reaction (+2.5%, July 2026) came with a raised guide; Jan 2026 -4.19% and Oct 2025 -1.91% came with the stock at or near highs.
findings.why_not_priced: This is about where the price sits, not a hidden fact. It is weak by construction: a de-rated stock is not by itself a reason to rise. It would be priced if the skew had turned to calls or the stock had already recovered to its 50-day MA (351.55); it has done neither.
findings.independence: S&P Global September bank-stock review: https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/articles/2026/10/most-us-bank-stocks-trade-lower-in-september-106462675. Price levels: https://www.marketpulse.com/markets/jpmorgan-q3-earnings-preview-can-strong-banking-momentum-continue/

findings.finding: Jefferies' fiscal Q3 (June-August 2026, reported 2026-09-28) was mixed. IB revenue was a record $1.33bn (+17%), with equity underwriting +69% and debt underwriting -21%. Equities were a record $626m (+29%), but fixed income fell 26%. FICC was ~60% of JPM's Q3'25 markets revenue ($5.6bn of $8.9bn), so the peer read supports the IB and equities lines and is a caution for FICC. It is net neutral against JPM's mid-to-high-teens markets guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Markets revenue beats have not lifted the stock by themselves (Q3'25: markets +25%, stock -1.91%).
findings.why_not_priced: Public peer print, but Jefferies' FICC is idiosyncratic and much smaller. It came out after JPM's 09-15 guide, so it is the one counterparty read later than the company's own remarks.

findings.finding: Expense risk on the call: the July guide was raised $2.5bn to ~$107.5bn, of which ~$1bn of volume-linked cost was implied for H2. A Q3 with IB and markets up mid-to-high teens brings more compensation accrual and a possible further nudge to the FY expense guide, or early 2027 expense signals. Expenses are the line that gave this stock its worst recent reactions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-12-09: -4.7% when Marianne Lake guided 2026 expense to ~$105bn against ~$101bn expected. 2026-01-13 print: -4.19%. July's +$2.5bn expense raise was absorbed by the NII raise (+2.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: A volume-linked expense rise sits inside what the company already flagged, so it is mostly priced. What is not priced is any early 2027 expense framing, which JPM usually saves for December and January; that is the tail.
findings.independence: July guide raise and its volume-linked composition: https://www.webull.com/news/15271033854174208

outside_window.finding: JPM typically gives its formal 2027 NII and expense outlook at the December industry conference and the Q4 print in January; the December 2025 expense guide moved the stock -4.7%.

Legal settlements, fines or one-off charges in Q3 2026: none found
Dimon's Bloomberg TV appearance around 2026-10-06: scheduled, but no coverage of what he said was found
Chase Issuance Trust September 2026 data: not yet published

rejected_candidates.candidate: BofA's Moynihan (2026-09-14) guided its own Q3 IB fees to $1.6-1.8bn vs $2.0bn and markets flat, saying the industry IB market was 'down 10% or so'. JPM fell 1.7% that day, then recovered on Petno's guide the next day.
rejected_candidates.detail: This is the peer contrast to JPM's own 09-15 guide and is already in that finding's bar; JPM's company-specific guide supersedes the peer industry read. BofA itself reports 2026-10-14, after the window.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Options-implied move of ±4.4% as of 2026-10-05, per MarketPulse, above JPM's 10-year average of ±3.4%.
rejected_candidates.detail: Duplicates the sealed baseline's option anchor (3.05% event / 3.36% straddle as of 2026-10-12), which is fresher and is used for abs_move.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Peers Wells Fargo, Citi and Goldman reportedly print the same morning (2026-10-13), and their reads will affect JPM's close.
rejected_candidates.detail: No content about those prints exists before the window; the dates are from aggregators. Not a finding, only a source of variance, which is reflected in abs_move.

baseline_tension: The slight positive lean (rotation-driven de-rating into an intact, guided-up quarter) runs against the mild put skew (+1.96) and against JPM's habit of selling beats (up on 1 of the last 4 prints), so p_up is held at 54 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 and 6 (verified fact is not a reaction; the finding lands inside what the company guided): the IB/markets guide finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.2, because JPM sold its Q3'25 above-guide beat (-1.91%).
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the LSEG-derived IB share finding rests on the same guided line, so it was cut from +0.2 to +0.15.

Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0; documents beat inference): the positioning/rotation finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.2. It has a sourced cause (fund flows, the Fed hike), so it was kept rather than zeroed.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxies filed small): the Fed-hike and H.8 findings were left at +0.3 and -0.3 as small proxies on opposite NII drivers, not contradictory.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (~1%, not crowded) before filing the expense and H.8 negatives; no change.
p_up and abs_move unchanged; the lessons moved only finding sizes, once each.
